pre_update_notes: The new per-product detail pages, IndexNow, and Bing sitemap ping all ship OFF/disabled by default — review and opt in from the new SEO Control Center (Settings → SEO) after updating, at your own pace. IMPORTANT for git-managed installs only (not zip/shared-hosting installs): this release fixes a bug where a git-managed self-update could delete the live .env file and the just-taken pre-update backup. That fix ships IN this release, so it protects every update FROM 1.0.17 onward — but the code that performs THIS SPECIFIC 1.0.16-to-1.0.17 update is still the old, unfixed 1.0.16 code (a self-updater cannot fix a bug in itself while using the buggy version to apply the very update that contains the fix). Any git-managed install updating from 1.0.16 (or earlier) to 1.0.17 should back up .env by hand first, purely as a precaution for this one hop.
post_update_notes: A full SEO program: every product can now get its own indexable detail page (/parts/{oem}/{id}-slug, opt-in) with an image gallery and cross-reference OEM numbers; cross-reference numbers are now sitemap- and autocomplete-discoverable; a verified-crawler bypass stops Googlebot/Bingbot from ever being rate-limited; redirect-loop detection now catches 3+ hop chains, not just direct reverse pairs; IndexNow, Bing sitemap ping, per-bot AI-crawler policy, and llms.txt are all new and admin-configurable; the old scattered SEO Settings page is replaced by one tabbed SEO Control Center, plus a new SEO Health Dashboard (search analytics, content health, feature adoption, IndexNow activity, redirect health, and optional Google Search Console / Core Web Vitals widgets once you add your own API credentials). Also includes global scheme/host/trailing-slash canonicalization, OPcache tuning, and a fix so settings changes (SMTP, OAuth credentials, session lifetime) take effect immediately on the long-running queue worker instead of only at its next restart. Every migration applies automatically; every new behavior defaults to matching what the site already did. See CHANGELOG.md for the full list.
